# SMKBBSP VisitorPass

> A school visitor management system for SMK Bandar Baru Sri Petaling. A visitor requests an
> appointment without an account and is shown a private link on screen; when the host teacher
> approves, that same link becomes an expiring QR pass. The system sends no email. At the gate a
> guard scans the pass, records that physical
> identification was sighted, and checks the visitor in. Visitor passes are digital only. Next.js App Router,
> TypeScript strict, PostgreSQL 16 via Prisma.

This file orients a language model working in this repository. Read it before making changes.
It is a map and a list of invariants, not a tutorial — the authoritative documents are linked below
and win any disagreement with this file.

## Read these first

- [docs/spec/PROJECT_SPEC.md](spec/PROJECT_SPEC.md): the product and technical contract. Highest authority.
- [docs/spec/ACCEPTANCE_TESTS.md](spec/ACCEPTANCE_TESTS.md): the executable definition of done (AT-001 to AT-030).
- [docs/spec/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md](spec/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md): build order and completion checklist.
- [docs/spec/FYP_SCOPE_REVISION.md](spec/FYP_SCOPE_REVISION.md): why the scope excludes what it excludes. Read before claiming any capability.
- [CLAUDE.md](../CLAUDE.md) and [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md): the engineering contract for agents.

On conflict, the priority is PROJECT_SPEC, then ACCEPTANCE_TESTS, then IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN, then
other prose.

## What this system deliberately is not

Do not add, simulate, or claim any of these. They were removed from the original proposal on
feasibility grounds and their absence is a graded property of the project:

MyDigitalID or any national identity SSO, Keycloak, biometrics of any kind, machine-learning
anomaly detection, licence-plate recognition, geofencing or location tracking, chatbots, paid
services required for the local demo, and production deployment.

**The single most important claim boundary:** the QR pass authorises *an approved appointment*.
It does not verify who the holder is. Identity assurance comes from a guard visually sighting
physical identification, which the system records as *a guard's declaration* — never as proof. OCR
reads text from a photograph to save typing; it does not verify identity and cannot detect a
forgery. Any wording that blurs this is a defect, including in comments and UI copy.

## Invariants that must not be broken

These are the rules most likely to be violated by an otherwise reasonable change.

**Identity data.** There is deliberately no column capable of holding a plaintext NRIC. Identity
numbers are stored as AES-256-GCM ciphertext plus a keyed HMAC (for blacklist matching and
de-duplication) plus the last four characters. Everything outside one explicit, audited admin
reveal shows the masked form. Build every identity column through `buildIdentityFields`
(`lib/crypto/identity.ts`) so normalisation, hashing and encryption cannot drift apart.

**Tokens.** Public, QR and session tokens are ≥256 bits of CSPRNG output and only ever stored
hashed. A QR encodes nothing but a pass URL whose variable part is an opaque token — no name,
identity number, host, purpose, or database id. The manual fallback code is *derived* from the
token hash (`deriveFallbackCode`) rather than stored, which is how the database keeps only a hash
while the pass page can still display the code.

**Four roles, and two different questions.** Administrators run the system; the principal reads it and changes nothing; guards work the gate; teachers see only their own queue and may approve or reject requests addressed to them. "May view the admin area" and "may change things" are separate checks - see OVERSIGHT_ROLES and canAdminister in lib/auth/authorize.ts. Every admin mutation asks for Role.ADMIN specifically, so hiding a control is never what stops a principal.

**Authorization is server-side.** Hiding a navigation link is not access control. Every protected
page and every mutation calls a helper from `lib/auth/authorize.ts` *before* fetching protected
data, so a denied request cannot briefly stream it. Teacher-scoped queries filter by `teacherId` in
the query itself, so a valid id belonging to another teacher matches nothing.

**Transactions and idempotency.** Approval, check-in, check-out and walk-in each write their status
change, visit, credential, in-app notifications and audit entry in one transaction, or none of them.
Repeating any of them returns the existing result rather than creating a second visit, badge,
credential or notification.

**No email.** The system sends nothing to anyone; there is no mail library installed and
`tests/unit/no-email.test.ts` fails if one is added. Staff are notified in-app
(`lib/domain/in-app-notifications.ts`), inside the business transaction. Visitors have no account:
submission redirects them to `/v/<token>`, the only place the raw token is ever shown.

**Never rotate the visitor's token on approval.** Approval binds the credential to the token issued
at submission. The visitor was shown that link once and nothing can be sent to them afterwards, so a
rotated link would strand an approved visitor. Only an administrator's reissue rotates it, and it
hands the new link back to that administrator. `decisions.test.ts` pins this end to end.

**Time.** Instants are stored in UTC and displayed in `Asia/Kuala_Lumpur`. Every "today", date range
and school-hours decision is evaluated against the Malaysian calendar day via `lib/time.ts`, never
the server's local day.

**Logging.** Never call `console` in application code; lint forbids it. Use `lib/logger.ts`, which
silences `debug`/`info` outside development and redacts every context object through the same
code the audit trail uses (`lib/redact.ts`). That redaction is what stops a casual
`log.debug('checking in', { visitor })` from leaking an identity number.

**Blacklist disclosure.** A guard sees only `CLEAR`, `REVIEW` or `BLOCKED` — never a reason,
category, or which field matched. A blocked visitor is shown a neutral "contact an administrator"
message. Name alone is never an automatic match.

## Where things live

```
app/                Next.js App Router. Server Components for reads,
                    server actions (`actions.ts` per area) for mutations.
  (public)          /, /login, /visit/request, /visit/status, /v/[token]
  teacher/          own queue and decisions only
  guard/            tablet-first gate operations, scan, walk-in, badge, emergency
  admin/            analytics, history, blacklist, users, settings, audit, reports
lib/
  auth/             session.ts (DB-backed, revocable), authorize.ts (role guards), login.ts
  crypto/           identity.ts (AES-GCM + HMAC), password.ts (scrypt), tokens.ts
  domain/           business services — the layer that owns transitions.
                    appointments, decisions, gate, credentials, blacklist, badges,
                    admin, analytics, settings, presenters, in-app-notifications
  reports/          query.ts shared by screen, pdf.ts and xlsx.ts
  redact.ts         one redactor, shared by audit and logger
  time.ts           UTC storage, Kuala Lumpur presentation
prisma/             schema.prisma, migrations/, seed.ts (deterministic, fictional)
tests/unit          pure logic: crypto, time, tokens, masking, parsing, escaping
tests/integration   real PostgreSQL, real transactions — no mocks
tests/e2e           Playwright, against a production build
scripts/            operational helpers, not application code
```

Domain services must not import React components. Keep business transitions in `lib/domain`, not in
pages.

## Commands

```bash
npm run dev            # development server
npm run lint           # ESLint
npm run typecheck      # tsc --noEmit
npm test               # Vitest: unit + integration (needs PostgreSQL)
npm run test:e2e       # prepares the E2E database, then Playwright
npm run build          # production build
npm run db:migrate     # create and apply a migration
npm run db:seed        # deterministic demonstration data
```

Run `lint`, `typecheck`, `test` and `build` before claiming any change is complete.

## Traps that have already caught someone

Each of these cost real debugging time. They are recorded so they cost it only once.

**A build, unit tests and `curl` all execute zero client JavaScript.** A strict `script-src 'self'`
once blocked every inline script Next.js uses to stream its RSC payload, so React never hydrated and
no server action could submit — while every check still reported green. The CSP is now issued
per-request with a nonce from `middleware.ts`; a static CSP header cannot carry a nonce. If you
change it, load a real page in a real browser against a **production** build.

**A blank screenshot in a failing browser test means hydration or CSP, not a bad selector.**

**Three databases** share one server: `visitorpass` (development), `visitorpass_test` (integration),
`visitorpass_e2e` (Playwright). A fresh volume contains only the first.

**Badge numbers** are unique but only random within a day. Allocate through `allocateBadgeNumber`,
which checks for collisions inside the transaction. A four-digit tail collides more often than
intuition suggests.

**The build must not need a database.** Routes reading settings or the session are `force-dynamic`
so nothing is prerendered against a database that may not exist.

**The lockfile is generated on Windows** and lacks Linux/musl variants of sharp's optional
dependencies, so Docker and CI use `npm install` rather than `npm ci`.

**Card reading is a vision model on an Ollama host, and it is server-side.** The browser posts a
photograph to `/api/ocr` (`app/api/ocr/route.ts`), which calls the model through
`lib/ocr/ollama.ts`. The browser never addresses the model host, which is what keeps
`connect-src 'self'` intact. This replaced a browser-side recognizer (PP-OCRv5 via ONNX Runtime)
because a classical recognizer transcribes lines and leaves a parser guessing which line was the
name, and a real laminated MyKad defeats that guess. Set `OCR_OLLAMA_URL` empty and the feature
disappears rather than failing at the moment somebody uses it.

**The model host is not the application server.** In the deployed system a laptop at the school
runs Ollama and the VPS reaches it over a Tailscale private network, so the photograph crosses a
WireGuard tunnel and never the public internet. This is the intended architecture rather than a
stopgap, and two things follow from it. Ollama has no authentication, so the tailnet is the entire
access control and the model port must never be published or forwarded. And the host is expected to
be offline sometimes - a laptop gets shut - so unavailability is a normal state that reports itself
and lets the form be typed, never something to retry or queue around. `HOSTING.md` has the setup,
including why the container needs the numeric `100.x` address rather than a MagicDNS name.

**Ollama's default context window is 4096 tokens regardless of the model's own limit**, and a
photographed card lands close enough to that ceiling to cross it depending on the picture. The host
then answers `400 exceed_context_size_error` rather than truncating, which surfaces as a failed
read of a perfectly good photograph. `lib/ocr/ollama.ts` therefore sets `num_ctx` explicitly. If
card reading starts failing on images that plainly ought to work, check that first.

**A language model fails differently, and the code is built around that.** A recognizer that
cannot read a digit returns something visibly wrong. A model returns a *fluent, well-formed*
identity number that nobody printed. There is no calibrated confidence to fall back on - asking a
model to rate its own certainty produces a number that reads well and means nothing - so the only
evidence used is whether a value could be real. `readIdentityNumber` knows a MyKad encodes a valid
birth date and an issued state code, and anything that fails it is returned as `null` rather than
flagged: a number that cannot be a MyKad is not worth showing a person at all. Never add a
confidence figure sourced from the model.

**The model's output is untrusted input.** It arrives as text that is *asked* to be JSON and
frequently is not - fenced, prefaced with prose, or truncated. `extractJsonObject` pulls the first
balanced object out (string-aware, so a brace inside a name cannot cut it short) and a Zod schema
discards everything else. Pin the model by name: an Ollama host can carry cloud-routed tags that
proxy to ollama.com — `gpt-oss:120b-cloud` is the published shape — and a loose model name would
eventually send someone's identity card to a third party. Two separate refusals cover this, and
they cover different mistakes. `isCloudRoutedModel` in `lib/env.ts` refuses a cloud tag at startup,
because the model-list check cannot: a cloud tag genuinely is installed on the host and so passes
it. `lib/ocr/ollama.ts` then checks the host's model list and refuses a name it does not find,
which is what stops a loose name resolving to whatever happens to be there.

**Only what the form can use is requested.** A card carries an address, a birthplace and a
religion; none have a field on the visitor form, so none are asked for. Extracting them would put
personal data in a server's memory - and possibly a log - for no purpose. The card *type* is the
one extra, and it is used solely to warn when a passport was photographed while the form says
MyKad.

**Frame voting is gone, and it was a real loss.** The camera still takes a burst, but only the
sharpest frame is sent. Voting across frames cancelled the random half of OCR error, because
sensor noise and hand shake differ per frame - but each frame is now a model call measured in
seconds, so three would mean half a minute at the gate and three times the rate-limit budget for
one scan. The blur warning in `lib/ocr/prepare-image.ts` is what remains of that safeguard.

**The card is not binarised before it is sent.** The preparation step used to threshold it to pure
black and white, which suited a classical recognizer. It is off-distribution input for a model
trained on ordinary photographs, and a threshold that clips a thin stroke deletes evidence
silently. `measureSharpness` reads the greyscale without touching the pixels for that reason.

## Data and privacy in this repository

The one image path. `/api/ocr` is the only endpoint that accepts an image. The photograph is held
for the length of one request, never written to disk, never cached and never logged, and nothing
read off the card is persisted - the identity number reaches the database only if the visitor
submits the form themselves, through the ordinary encrypted path. There is no upload directory and
nothing should create one.

All seeded people, contacts and identity numbers are invented. Email addresses use the reserved
`.test` TLD, which cannot resolve on the public internet. No real staff member, student or parent
appears anywhere. Keep it that way: use fictional data in fixtures, tests, screenshots and reports,
and never commit a real `.env`.
